newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia likely to get $600 mln loan from World Bank.
newsitem.headline: Russia likely to get $600 mln loan from World Bank.

text.p: Russia is likely to get a $600 million credit from the World Bank to restructure the economy, Interfax news agency quoted Minister without Portfolio Yevgeny Yasin as saying on Monday.
Yasin, who acts as economic guru to the government, said he hoped the World Bank's board of directors would approve the loan when it met on June 5, Interfax said.
"The credit is very important for us, as it will be channelled to replenish the budget and make timely social payments," Interfax quoted Yasin as saying.

Interfax said six World Bank directors had arrived in Russia to monitor the course of economic reforms and the way Russia uses earlier World Bank credits. The delegation plans to visit coal regions this week to check restructuring in the industry.
Russia also hopes to get another $500 million loan to restructure the coal industry, Interfax said.
However the World Bank's decision would be tied to the way Russia used the previous $500 million loan to the coal industry, Yasin told Interfax.
He said Russia had failed to fulfil some of the terms of the previous credit, including the one on transferring some of the biggest mines into trust to commercial companies.
But Yasin said he managed to convince World Bank officials that Russia had succeeded in restructuring the coal industry.

Russian daily Sevodnya said in its Monday issue that the government plans to hold a trust tender for Bashkirugol mine in May and a trust tender for Vostsibugol mine in Irkutsk region in mid-June. The two mines account for eight percent of Russia's coal output.

The government also plans to approve the schedule of trust tenders for Kuzbassrazrezugol, Yuzhny Kuzbass and Krasnoyarskugol mines before May 15, Sevodnya said. The results of the tenders will be announced before July 20.
